title: Rocks & Soil
description: Grade 3 Science: rocks and soil — kinds of rocks, how soil is made, the layers of soil, and why soil matters. Label the soil layers and do a soil-jar experiment.

topics.title: The Ground Beneath Us
topics.concept:
Everything we stand on is part of the Earth's surface. Just below us are two important things:

  • 🪨 Rocks — hard, solid pieces of the Earth. Mountains, pebbles and sand all come from rock.
  • 🟫 Soil — the loose top layer where plants grow. It is made of tiny bits of rock mixed with dead leaves and tiny living things.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="150" fill="#f3efe6"/><rect width="300" height="40" fill="#7ec850"/><rect y="40" width="300" height="50" fill="#8a5a2a"/><rect y="90" width="300" height="60" fill="#9aa0a6"/><text x="150" y="32" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle">🌳</text><text x="150" y="70" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#fff" text-anchor="middle">Soil</text><text x="150" y="126" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#fff" text-anchor="middle">Rock</text></svg>
recap: Below us is rock and soil.
Rocks are hard, solid pieces of the Earth.
Soil is the loose top layer where plants grow.

wonder.text: Under the grass, the roads and your house lies a hidden world of rock and soil. What is it made of?

qa.a: Yes! Mountains are giant masses of solid rock. Over millions of years, wind and water slowly wear them down into smaller rocks, pebbles and sand.

qa.q: Is sand a kind of rock?
qa.a: Yes — sand is just millions of tiny grains of rock, worn down very small by water and wind over a very long time.

topics.title: Different Kinds of Rocks
topics.concept:
Rocks come in many colours, shapes and hardness. Some are useful in special ways:

  • 🧱 Hard, strong rocks like granite are used to build houses and roads.
  • ✏️ Some soft rocks are used to make chalk and pencil 'lead'.
  • 💎 Some rocks hold shiny gems and useful metals like iron and gold.
  • 🪨 River pebbles are smooth; mountain rocks are rough.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="150" fill="#f3efe6"/><text x="55" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🪨</text><text x="55" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Hard rock</text><text x="165" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🧱</text><text x="165" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Building</text><text x="275" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">💎</text><text x="275" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Gems</text><text x="165" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Rocks come in many kinds</text></svg>
recap: Rocks vary in colour, shape and hardness.
Hard rocks build houses; some rocks hold metals and gems.
River pebbles are smooth; mountain rocks are rough.

wonder.text: A smooth river pebble and a rough, sparkly stone are both rocks. Why are rocks so different?

qa.a: As pebbles tumble along in the moving river water for a long time, their rough edges get worn away. Slowly they become smooth and round.

qa.q: Where do we get metals like iron?
qa.a: Metals are found inside certain rocks deep in the ground. People dig them out from mines and then take the metal out of the rock.

topics.title: How Soil Is Made
topics.concept:
Soil is made very slowly, over a very long time, in these steps:

  • 🪨 Big rocks are broken by Sun, rain, wind and ice (this is called weathering).
  • 🪨 They break into smaller and smaller pieces — pebbles, then grains.
  • 🍂 Dead leaves, plants and tiny creatures mix in and rot.
  • 🟫 Together they make rich, dark soil where plants can grow.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 130" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="130" fill="#f3efe6"/><text x="45" y="66" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🪨</text><defs><marker id="sm3" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#a4724a"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#a4724a" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#sm3)"><line x1="72" y1="58" x2="118" y2="58"/></g><text x="150" y="66" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle">🌧️</text><text x="150" y="96" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="10" font-weight="700" fill="#7a5b3a" text-anchor="middle">weather</text><g stroke="#a4724a" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#sm3)"><line x1="182" y1="58" x2="228" y2="58"/></g><text x="270" y="66" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🟫</text><text x="160" y="122" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#7a5b3a" text-anchor="middle">Rock → weathering → soil</text></svg>
recap: Soil forms very slowly over a long time.
Weather breaks rock into tiny bits (weathering).
Rotted leaves and plants mix in to make rich soil.

wonder.text: Soil takes hundreds of years to form. How does hard rock turn into soft soil?

qa.a: Weathering is the slow breaking of rocks by the weather — heat, rain, wind and ice. Over many years it crumbles big rocks into tiny bits.
Rich soil is dark because it has lots of rotted leaves and plant bits mixed in. This makes it full of food for plants — perfect for growing.

topics.title: Layers of the Soil
topics.concept:
If we dig down, we find soil is made of layers, one below another:

  • 🌱 Topsoil — the dark, rich top layer. Plants' roots grow here. It has the most food for plants.
  • 🟫 Subsoil — a lighter, harder layer below, with more stones and fewer roots.
  • 🪨 Bedrock — solid, hard rock at the very bottom.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 240" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Layers of soil: topsoil, subsoil and bedrock"><rect width="300" height="240" fill="#a47148"/><rect width="300" height="30" fill="#7ec850"/><rect y="30" width="300" height="80" fill="#5a3a1a"/><rect y="110" width="300" height="70" fill="#a47148"/><rect y="180" width="300" height="60" fill="#8a8d91"/><g stroke="#3f8a2f" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"><line x1="150" y1="30" x2="150" y2="4"/><line x1="150" y1="14" x2="138" y2="4"/><line x1="150" y1="14" x2="162" y2="4"/></g><g stroke="#3a2410" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none"><path d="M150 30 L140 60 M150 30 L160 65 M150 30 L150 80"/></g><g fill="#7d7f83"><circle cx="80" cy="140" r="6"/><circle cx="210" cy="150" r="7"/><circle cx="130" cy="160" r="5"/></g><g stroke="#6f7276" stroke-width="2"><line x1="40" y1="205" x2="110" y2="205"/><line x1="160" y1="220" x2="250" y2="220"/></g></svg>
recap: Soil has layers: topsoil, subsoil and bedrock.
Topsoil is dark and rich — plants' roots grow here.
Bedrock is the solid hard rock at the bottom.

wonder.text: Dig deep into the ground and you pass through different layers. What changes as you go down?

qa.q: Why do plant roots stay in the topsoil?
qa.a: The topsoil is soft, dark and full of food and water for plants. So most roots spread out in this top layer where they can drink and feed easily.

qa.q: What is right at the bottom?
qa.a: At the very bottom is bedrock — solid, hard rock. It is too hard for roots, and the whole soil sits on top of it.

topics.title: Why Soil Matters
topics.concept:
Soil is one of nature's greatest treasures. It does so much for us:

  • 🌾 Plants and crops grow in it — giving us food.
  • 💧 It soaks up rain water and stores it.
  • 🐛 It is home to worms, insects and tiny living things.
  • 🌳 It holds tree roots firmly in place.

We must protect soil — too much cutting of trees can wash good soil away. Plants and trees hold the soil and keep it healthy.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="150" fill="#eef9f1"/><rect y="80" width="300" height="70" fill="#8a5a2a"/><text x="150" y="60" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🌱</text><text x="90" y="120" font-size="26" text-anchor="middle">🐛</text><text x="220" y="118" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle">💧</text><text x="150" y="144" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#fff" text-anchor="middle">Soil grows our food</text></svg>
recap: Soil grows our food and stores rain water.
It is home to worms and tiny creatures.
Trees hold soil in place — cutting them causes soil to wash away.

wonder.text: Without soil, there would be no wheat, no rice, no vegetables. How does soil feed the whole world?

qa.q: How do earthworms help the soil?
qa.a: Earthworms tunnel through soil, letting in air and water, and their waste makes the soil richer. They are tiny farmers' friends that keep soil healthy!

qa.q: How does cutting trees harm soil?
qa.a: Tree roots hold the soil in place. When too many trees are cut, rain and wind wash the good topsoil away. This is called soil erosion.

questions.q: Soil is the loose top layer where…
questions.explanation: Soil is the loose top layer where plants grow.

questions.q: The dark, rich top layer of soil is called…
questions.explanation: Topsoil is the dark, rich top layer where roots grow.
Sand is millions of tiny grains of rock.

questions.q: The slow breaking of rocks by weather is called…
questions.explanation: Weathering is rocks being broken by Sun, rain, wind and ice.

questions.q: The hard, solid rock at the bottom of the soil is…
questions.explanation: Bedrock is the solid, hard rock at the very bottom.

questions.q: Which creature helps make soil healthy?
questions.explanation: Earthworms tunnel through soil and make it richer.

questions.q: Why are river pebbles smooth and round?
options: Moving water wears their edges away over time
questions.explanation: Tumbling in moving river water slowly wears the pebbles smooth.

questions.q: Why do most plant roots stay in the topsoil?
options: It is soft, dark and full of food and water
questions.explanation: Topsoil is soft and rich in food and water, perfect for roots.

questions.q: How does cutting too many trees harm the soil?
options: Roots no longer hold the soil, so it washes away (erosion)
questions.explanation: Tree roots hold soil in place; without them, soil washes away — soil erosion.

questions.q: In a shaken soil-and-water jar, what settles at the BOTTOM first?
questions.explanation: The heaviest bits — sand and stones — sink to the bottom first.

questions.q: Put in order how soil forms.
options: Big rock → weathering → tiny bits → soil
questions.explanation: Big rocks are weathered into tiny bits that mix with dead plants to form soil.
